name: Projected Maximum Positive Degree
definition: The **Projected Maximum Positive Degree** is $$\mathrm{d}^{+p}_{\max}(\mathcal H)\bydef\max_{S\subseteq\mathcal X}\mathrm{d}^{+}_{\max}(\mathcal H_{|S}),$$ the largest maximum positive degree among coordinate projections.
graph_summary: Largest maximum positive degree attained by a coordinate projection.
description: The projection-monotonic closure of maximum positive degree.
origin_references: Database-defined projection closure of the oriented one-inclusion-graph parameter.

monotonic.proof: For every coordinate set S, a trace of a subfamily is a subfamily of the corresponding trace. Maximum positive degree is subfamily-monotonic, and taking maxima preserves the inequality.

p_monotonic.proof: Every projection of a projection of H is already a projection of H, so the maximum over traces cannot increase after projection.

c_monotonic.proof: A conditioned fibre is a subfamily followed by a projection, so doubly monotonicity implies conditioning monotonicity.

doubly_monotonic.proof: The preceding subfamily and projection arguments establish both required forms.
